record.paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
record.context_brief: stability of KSW-narrow operators under addition
record.original_question: For an arbitrary Banach space X, is the sum of two KSW-narrow operators in L(L1[0,1], X) again KSW-narrow?

evidence.quote: Problem 20. ([59]) For any Banach space X , is the sum of two KSW-narrow operators from L(L1, X) also KSW-narrow (cf. Problem 18)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L_1=L_1[0,1]$ denote the space of Lebesgue integrable functions on $[0,1]$ with its usual norm. For a Banach space $X$, denote by $L(L_1,X)$ the space of bounded linear operators from $L_1$ into $X$.

A bounded linear operator $T\in L(L_1,X)$ is called KSW-narrow (in the sense of Kadets–Shvidkovsky–Werner) if for every measurable set $A\subseteq[0,1]$ of positive measure and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a measurable subset $B\subseteq A$ with $\mu(B)=\tfrac12\mu(A)$ such that
$$\bigl\|T(\mathbf{1}_A-2\mathbf{1}_B)\bigr\|_X<\varepsilon,$$
equivalently, $T$ maps suitable mean‑zero sign functions supported in $A$ to vectors of arbitrarily small norm.

Question: Is it true that for every Banach space $X$ and every pair of KSW-narrow operators $T_1,T_2\in L(L_1[0,1],X)$, the sum $T_1+T_2$ is again KSW-narrow?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that for several standard notions of narrow operators on $L_1$, the sum of two narrow operators is known to be narrow, and there are recent papers (e.g., "On sums of narrow and compact operators", Positivity 2019) extending such stability results. However, no source was located that explicitly resolves the specific stability question for KSW-narrow operators from $L_1[0,1]$ into an arbitrary Banach space, so the present status of this precise question could not be confirmed.

status_evidence.title: On sums of narrow and compact operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when sums of narrow operators (and narrow plus compact) remain narrow on Köthe Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses stability of narrowness under addition, but does not explicitly settle the KSW-narrow case on L1 to arbitrary X.

status_evidence.title: Narrow operators and rich subspaces of Banach spaces with the Daugavet property
status_evidence.snippet: Kadets, Shvidkoy, Werner introduce the notion of narrow operator used in the question.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the definition of KSW-narrow operator referenced in the problem.
